finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::app token in the ci-fix job is minted with no permission scoping, then handed to the llm fixer this diff enables
evidence: Confirmed in the supplied `agent-iterate-ci.yml`: the `Generate GitHub App token` step (~line 55-60, not 93 as claimed) passes only `app-id`/`private-key`, so the token inherits the installation's full permission set; the subsequent `actions/checkout` sets `token:` without `persist-credentials: false`, and the same token is handed to `claude-code-action` as `github_token` (~line 154, matching the diff hunk at 152) in a job that runs `pnpm install` and an unrestricted-`Bash` agent. The asymmetry is verifiable: the `fix` job in `agent-review-panel.yml` mints the same App token with `permission-contents/pull-requests/issues` and explicitly comments that it is "used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code," so the missing scoping here is a genuine least-privilege gap, and the diff's `allowed_bots` addition is indeed what lets the fixer step execute rather than abort on the bot-actor check. The claim's line numbers are all wrong for this revision and two cited comparison files (`agent-fix.yml`, `agent-review-on-demand.yml`) don't exist here, but the substance holds. I rate it minor rather than major because the incremental capability over the contents/PR write the job already requires depends on the App installation's granted permissions, which are not visible in the repo, and the pipeline is inert unless `AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED` is set; note also that the unscoped mint is pre-existing code the diff does not touch.
